mainTopic: רבי אלעזר's reason for permitting the צרה, and the rules for identifying a dead man by his face and by סימנים
overview: The amud opens by asking what difference it makes which reason stands behind רבי אלעזר's ruling. One possible reason is צרה מעידה לחברתה. The other is that the woman would not ruin herself by marrying if her husband were alive. The difference is whether her צרה may marry before she herself marries. Two proofs are brought from רבי אלעזר's words, and both are pushed away. The first is answered with 'לדבריהם קאמר'. The second is answered by reading 'permitted and married', and that reading is then defended by placing the case where she married a כהן. The רבנן reject the whole idea, because she might act like שמשון: 'תמות נפשי עם פלשתים'. A new משנה then teaches that one may testify that a man died only after seeing his face with the nose, seeing that he actually died, and seeing the body within three days. רבי יהודה בן בבא disagrees with the fixed three-day limit. The גמרא explains the face requirement with a ברייתא, a פסוק and the story of אבא בר מרתא. It then asks whether סימנים are valid by Torah law. אביי answers that this is a מחלוקת תנאים about a mole, and רבא gives several versions explaining that מחלוקת differently, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The practical difference: may the rival wife marry first?
steps.stepSummary: The two possible reasons for רבי אלעזר lead to different results when the rival wife wants to marry before the woman who testified has married.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether we let the rival wife marry before the testifying woman marries. If the reason is that a rival wife can testify for her fellow wife, the rival may marry even before the testifier marries. If the reason is that the testifier would not ruin herself, the rival may marry only once the testifier has married. Until then, the rival may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question 'what difference does it make which reason is right?' by pointing to a real case where the two reasons give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman is simply believed about her rival (צרה מעידה לחברתה), her word alone is enough, so the rival can marry right away. If the only guarantee is that she would not ruin herself, that guarantee exists only once she has actually married on the strength of her own claim. Before that, she might be lying just to trap her rival.

keyTerms.meaning: A rival wife: another wife of the same husband
Testifies for her fellow wife (is believed about her)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two women here. 'She' who married or didn't is the woman who testified that the husband died. The one we are deciding about is her צרה, the rival wife.

phrases.english: To let the rival wife marry before her:
If you say a rival wife may testify for her fellow wife,
even though she has not married,
we let the rival wife marry.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם דְּהִיא לָא מְקַלְקְלָא נַפְשַׁהּ,
phrases.english: If you say it is because she would not ruin herself,
then if she married, we let the rival wife marry;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא אִינְּסִיב — לָא מַנְסְבִינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: if she has not married, we do not let her marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question (just before this section) about the practical difference between the two reasons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between 'a rival may testify for her fellow' and 'she would not ruin herself'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether the rival wife may marry before the testifying woman has married.

steps.title: So which reason is right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two reasons is actually רבי אלעזר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: This one-word question sets up the next step: now that we know the reasons give different results, the גמרא wants to know which one רבי אלעזר holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having shown that the two reasons lead to different halachic results, the גמרא now has a real reason to decide between them.

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: He's asking which of the two reasons רבי אלעזר holds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the practical difference and asks for the decision.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason רבי אלעזר actually holds.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אלעזר's wording: they already married
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר speaks of women who were already permitted to the יבמין, meaning they already married. That fits the reason 'she would not ruin herself', so the גמרא concludes this is his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר says, 'Since they were permitted to the יבמין, they are permitted to everyone.' If his reason is that she would not ruin herself, it makes sense that he speaks of a case where she already married. But if his reason is that a rival wife may testify for her fellow wife, the rival should be allowed to marry even when the testifier has not married! So learn from this that רבי אלעזר's reason is that she has married and would not ruin herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove which reason רבי אלעזר holds from the exact case he chose to talk about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר speaks only about women who already married the יבמין. If testimony alone were enough (צרה מעידה לחברתה), there would be no need to wait for that marriage. So the detail 'they married' seems to show that the actual marriage is what makes us trust her.

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר says:
Since they were permitted to the brothers-in-law,
they are permitted to any man.
It makes sense if you say
that she would not ruin herself:
that is why, when she married, we let her rival marry,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם דְּצָרָה מְעִידָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ —
phrases.english: but if you say it is because a rival wife may testify for her fellow wife,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִינְּסִיב נָמֵי!
phrases.english: then even if she has not married, the rival should also be allowed!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rather, learn from this that רבי אלעזר's reason

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִינְּסִיב הוּא, וְלָא מְקַלְקְלָא נַפְשַׁהּ.
phrases.english: is because she has married, and she would not ruin herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר's reason is 'she would not ruin herself'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's own wording, which speaks of women already permitted to (married to) the יבמין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר was arguing on the רבנן's own terms
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבי אלעזר personally holds צרה מעידה לחברתה, but he chose a case the רבנן should agree to even on their own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר was speaking to the רבנן according to their own view: 'In my view, a rival wife may testify for her fellow wife, and even if she has not married, we let the rival marry. But in your view, at least admit to me that where she has married, we let the rival marry, because she would not ruin herself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. רבי אלעזר's choice of a 'married' case does not show his own reason. He was just picking the case most convincing to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's own position may be the broader one, that the rival can marry even before. He argued from the narrower case because it uses the רבנן's own logic against them. So the wording proves nothing about his personal reason.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their (the other side's) words

steps.confusionAlert: 'לדבריהם' does not mean רבי אלעזר changed his mind. He still holds his own view and is only arguing from the other side's starting point.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר was speaking to them according to their own view:
In my view, a rival wife may testify for her fellow wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִינְּסִיב — מַנְסְבִינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: and even if she has not married, we let the rival marry.
But in your view, at least admit to me
that where she has married, we let the rival marry,
because she would not ruin herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question of רבי אלעזר's reason stays open, and he may hold צרה מעידה לחברתה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי אלעזר's case shows his own reason, but he may have chosen it only to persuade the רבנן on their terms.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'לדבריהם קאמר' is a common גמרא tool: a speaker's choice of case can be a debating move rather than his full view.

steps.title: Why the רבנן still disagree: 'Let me die with the Philistines'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not accept even the narrower argument. A woman might marry, harming herself, just to harm her rival.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say she acts on the idea 'Let me die with the Philistines': she may hurt herself in order to hurt her rival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן still forbid even after the woman married. They do not accept that she would never ruin herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's argument rested on 'she would not ruin herself'. The רבנן answer that hatred of a rival can push a woman to harm herself too, like שמשון bringing the house down on himself and the פלשתים. So her own marriage does not prove she is telling the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let me die with the Philistines': שמשון's words, harming oneself to harm the enemy

steps.whatToRemember: Two possible reasons for רבי אלעזר: (1) צרה מעידה לחברתה, so the rival may marry even before; (2) she would not ruin herself, so only after she married. The proof for (2) is rejected because רבי אלעזר spoke לדבריהם. The רבנן reject even (2): 'תמות נפשי עם פלשתים'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
she acts on 'Let me die with the Philistines.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, ״תָּמוֹת נַפְשִׁי עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּים״ הוּא דְּקָעָבְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to the argument רבי אלעזר made on their terms in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן hold that a woman may harm herself in order to harm her rival, so even her own marriage does not make her rival permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא where the rival is permitted as soon as the wife is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר: since the wife who testified is permitted, her צרה is permitted too. This sounds like the צרה may marry even before the wife marries.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A woman went overseas with her husband. She came back and said, 'My husband died.' She may marry and collect her כתובה, but her rival wife is forbidden. רבי אלעזר says: since she is permitted, her rival wife is permitted too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to settle which of the two reasons belongs to רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says the צרה is permitted 'since she is permitted.' He does not say 'since she married.' That suggests the צרה may marry right away, which would not fit the reason 'she would not ruin herself.' That reason needs the wife to have actually married first.

keyTerms.meaning: A country overseas, far away, where no one else saw what happened
Rival wife: the other wife of the same husband

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A woman who went, she and her husband,
to a country overseas,
and she came back and said: "My husband died"
she may marry and collect her marriage contract,
but her rival wife is forbidden.
Rabbi Elazar says:
Since she is permitted,
her rival wife is also permitted.
phrases.notes: The key point: he only says she is 'permitted,' not that she has already married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to settle the question from Step 2, after the earlier proof was pushed off.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר's reason does not depend on the wife having already married
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'הוֹאִיל וְהוּתְּרָה הִיא הוּתְּרָה נָמֵי צָרָתָהּ'

steps.title: Read it as permitted and already married
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It reads רבי אלעזר's words as 'since she was permitted and has married.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: since she was permitted and married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by adding words to רבי אלעזר's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'permitted and married,' the ברייתא fits the reason 'she would not ruin herself' after all. So the ברייתא does not prove which reason is רבי אלעזר's.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the words this way instead

phrases.english: Say:
Since she was permitted and has married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 6 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא only; the ברייתא itself still stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as speaking about a wife who already married, so it fits either reason.

steps.title: Maybe she was really divorced and wants to trap her rival
steps.stepSummary: Even if the wife married, there is a worry. Maybe she came back with a גט and is lying about the death just to make her צרה marry a man who is still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry: maybe she came back with a גט. When she says 'he died,' maybe she only means to ruin her rival wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading. Her marrying does not prove the husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced woman may marry too, so her marrying causes her no harm even if the husband is alive. She could claim he died only so that her צרה would marry and end up in a forbidden marriage. So 'she would not ruin herself' does not help here.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us worry about this possibility
To ruin her, to get her into trouble

steps.confusionAlert: Here the wife's own marriage is fine. The harm the גמרא worries about falls only on the צרה, who would remarry while the husband is alive.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps
she came with a bill of divorce,
and the fact that she says this,
she intends to ruin her rival wife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from Step 7. Her marrying alone does not show she is telling the truth.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'since she was permitted and married'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorcee may also marry, so her marrying costs her nothing. It gives no proof that the husband is dead, and the צרה could be trapped.

steps.title: She married a כהן, so she must be a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the worry is real if she married a ישראל. But the case is that she married a כהן, and a divorcee may not marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married a ישראל, yes, that worry is real. Here we are dealing with a case where she married a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry by narrowing the case to a wife who married a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרושה is forbidden to a כהן, but a widow is allowed. If she really had a גט, marrying a כהן would harm her. Since she would not harm herself, her marrying a כהן shows the husband really died, and the צרה may marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed so: the גמרא agrees with the worry in that case
Here what case are we dealing with: the case is being narrowed
A כהן, who may not marry a divorced woman

steps.whatToRemember: According to the reason 'she would not ruin herself,' the צרה may marry only after the wife has married in a way that would hurt her if she were lying, for example by marrying a כהן.

phrases.english: If she married a regular Israelite,
indeed so (we would worry).
phrases.notes: A divorced woman may marry a regular Jew, so that marriage proves nothing.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where she married a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry in Step 8 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any marriage by the wife would count, so a lie about a גט could trap the צרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a wife who married a כהן. A divorcee could not do that, so she must truly be a widow.

steps.title: New משנה: identification needs the face with the nose
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that one may testify that a man died only after recognizing his face together with the nose. Signs on his body or his belongings are not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may testify only about the face together with the nose. Even if there are identifying signs on his body or his belongings, that is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rules for identifying a dead man so that his wife may remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the full face with the nose counts as sure identification. Marks on the body or on his clothes and belongings do not count on their own, even though they seem to point to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: a new משנה starts here

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may testify only
about the face together with the nose.
Even though there are identifying signs
on his body and on his belongings,
phrases.notes: The words 'one may not testify' at the start of the next line go with this too: these signs aren't enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַל פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים עִם הַחוֹטֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the discussion of רבי אלעזר ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony about a man's death needs a view of his face with the nose. Body marks or belongings alone are not enough.

steps.title: He must have truly died, and the body must be seen within three days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds two rules. One may not testify until the man has actually died, even if he looked sure to die. And identification counts only within three days after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not testify until his soul leaves him. Even if they saw him cut up, or hanging on a cross, or with a wild animal eating him, one may not testify. And one may testify only up to three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with when testimony about death is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being badly wounded, crucified, or attacked by an animal is not proof of death, because the man might still survive. A separate rule limits testimony to seeing the body within three days after death. After that, the face may change and no longer be clearly recognized, which is the point רבי יהודה בן בבא picks up in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Until his soul leaves him: until he actually dies

steps.whatToRemember: To permit a woman whose husband is said to have died, the witness must have recognized the face with the nose, seen that he truly died, and seen the body within three days.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: One may not testify until his soul has departed.
And even if they saw him cut up or crucified
or with a wild animal eating him,
one may not testify (that he died).
And one may testify only up to three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more conditions for testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony is accepted only after actual death, not just deadly wounds, and only if the body was seen within three days.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא: bodies change at different speeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בבא disagrees with a fixed three-day limit, because people, places and times are not all the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בבא says: Not every person, not every place and not every hour is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי יהודה בן בבא, who says you cannot set one fixed time limit for recognizing a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said identification counts only within three days. רבי יהודה בן בבא answers that how fast a body changes depends on the person, the place and the time. So one rule cannot fit every case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava says:
Not every person,
nor every place,
nor every hour is the same.
phrases.notes: He means a body changes faster or slower depending on the situation, so 'three days' can't be a fixed rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing view on the three-day limit from step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no single fixed time limit for identifying a body. It depends on the person, the place and the time.

steps.title: ברייתא: forehead, face and nose are all needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a witness must see the forehead and the face, together with the nose, before testifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: If the witness saw the forehead but not the face, or the face but not the forehead, he may not testify. He must see both of them together with the nose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that explains exactly what 'the face' in the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said only that the witness must recognize the face with the nose. The ברייתא adds detail: the forehead and the main features of the face are both needed, along with the nose. Seeing only part of the face is not enough.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
If he saw the forehead but not the features of the face,
or the features of the face but not the forehead,
they may not testify,
until both of them are seen together with the nose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's 'face with the nose' rule from step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony needs the forehead, the facial features and the nose, all seen together.

steps.title: The verse that shows the face is the way to recognize someone
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב כהנא) brings a פסוק showing that a person is truly recognized by his face.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב כהנא: What is the verse? 'The recognition of their faces testifies against them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for the rule that you must see the face to identify someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the face itself 'testifies' about a person. This shows that the face is the real way to know who someone is. That is why the ברייתא requires the face and not other signs.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Kahana:
What is the verse?
"The recognition of their faces testifies against them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the face requirement in step 13
steps.raayaObject: The rule that identification depends on seeing the face

steps.title: אבא בר מרתא hides his forehead and is not recognized
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that covering just the forehead can stop people from recognizing someone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא בר מרתא, who is אבא בר מניומי, owed money to the people of the ריש גלותא's house. He took wax, stuck it onto a worn rag, and stuck that on his forehead. He walked right past them, and they did not recognize him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how important the forehead is for recognizing a face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא בר מרתא only changed how his forehead looked, yet people who knew him did not recognize him. This supports the ברייתא in step 13, which says seeing the face without the forehead is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia

steps.whatToRemember: To testify that a man died, the witness must see his whole face: forehead, features and nose. Even a small change to the forehead can make a person look like someone else.

phrases.english: Abba bar Marta,
who is Abba bar Minyumi,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַסְּקִי בֵּיהּ דְּבֵי רֵישָׁא גָּלוּתָא זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: owed money to the people of the Exilarch's house.
He brought wax,
stuck it onto a worn rag,
and stuck that on his forehead.
He passed in front of them
and they did not recognize him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא דְּהוּא אַבָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example that supports the forehead requirement
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the forehead is needed to identify a face
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which Abba bar Marta covered his forehead and was not recognized

steps.title: Does the משנה mean identifying signs are not from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that signs are not enough and asks whether this means סימנים are not valid by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Even though there are signs, etc.' Does this mean that signs are not valid by Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה and asks what it shows. This question sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that signs on the body or on the clothing do not allow testimony. The גמרא asks whether this means סימנים are not trusted by Torah law at all. That is a big claim, because סימנים are used in other areas of הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, by Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as the final ruling. The גמרא is only asking what the משנה implies. The answer comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether סימנים count by Torah law matters far beyond this case, for example in returning lost objects.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִימָנִין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "Even though there are signs, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה from step 10.

phrases.english: Is this to say that signs
are not valid by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about signs and opens a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה's rejection of signs show that סימנים are not valid by Torah law?

steps.title: A lost גט identified by signs is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where a שליח who lost a גט may still deliver it if he finds it tied to something recognizable. This suggests that סימנים work even by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: If he found it tied to a purse, a money bag or a ring, or it was found among his belongings, even after a long time, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from Step 16 that סימנים are only rabbinic. It quotes a ברייתא that relies on signs to identify a lost גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט lets a married woman remarry, and that is a Torah-level matter. If we may identify a lost גט just by the purse or ring it was tied to, then סימנים must be trusted by Torah law. That clashes with the משנה, which says signs are not enough to identify a dead man.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (one source against another)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
If he found it tied to a purse
phrases.notes: "It" is a גט that the messenger lost on the way to the woman.

phrases.english: or to a money bag, or to a ring,
or it was found among his belongings,
even after a long time, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading raised in Step 16, that סימנים are not valid by Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that signs are not enough to identify a dead man, read as meaning סימנים are only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט is a Torah-level matter, yet the ברייתא relies on signs to identify it. So סימנים must be valid by Torah law.

steps.title: אביי says the two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that there is no contradiction. The ברייתא about the גט follows רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying each source follows a different תנא. He proves this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not try to make the משנה and the ברייתא agree. He accepts that they disagree and explains that each one follows a different opinion about סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one ... that one (pointing to two different sources)

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
this one follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Mahavai,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the ברייתא about the lost גט.

phrases.english: that one follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "That one" is our משנה, which says signs are not enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: the two sources follow two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא should agree, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different opinions: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי, and the משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The מחלוקת about testifying based on a mole
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא where the תנא קמא says not to testify based on a mole, and רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי says one may. He suggests they disagree about whether סימנים are Torah-level or rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One may not testify based on a mole. רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי says: One may testify. Is it not that they disagree about this, that one holds סימנים are Torah-level and the other holds סימנים are rabbinic?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the source for his answer: a ברייתא showing a real מחלוקת between תנאים about identifying someone by a mole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mole is a type of סימן. The רבנן do not allow testimony based on it, so they must hold סימנים are only rabbinic. רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי allows it, so he must hold they are Torah-level, which fits the ברייתא about the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: A mole or birthmark on the body
Is it not that... (a suggested reading, which may later be rejected)
Identifying signs are valid by Torah law
Identifying signs are valid only by rabbinic law

phrases.english: As it was taught: One may not testify based on a mole.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן מַהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר: מְעִידִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Mahavai says: One may testify.
Is it not about this that they disagree:
that one Sage holds signs are valid by Torah law,
phrases.notes: This "one Sage" is רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי, who allows testimony based on a mole.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds signs are only rabbinic?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in Step 18 with a ברייתא showing a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a מחלוקת תנאים about whether סימנים are Torah-level.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about testifying based on a mole: the תנא קמא forbids it, and רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי allows it.

steps.title: רבא says the question is whether such a mole is common
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's reading of the ברייתא. Everyone agrees סימנים are Torah-level; they disagree about whether a similar mole is often found on someone like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that סימנים are valid by Torah law. Here they disagree about whether such a mole is commonly found on his peer. One Sage holds it is commonly found on his peer, and the other holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof from Step 19 by giving a different reason for the מחלוקת about the mole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the תנא קמא does not reject סימנים in general. He only says a mole is a weak sign because many similar people have one. So the mole ברייתא is no longer a proof that some תנאים hold סימנים are only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: His peer, someone of his age and similar to him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סִימָנִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
phrases.english: Rava said: Everyone agrees that signs are valid by Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, בְּשׁוּמָא מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: Here, they disagree about whether a mole is commonly found on his peer.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: שׁוּמָא מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: a mole is commonly found on his peer,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אֵינָהּ מְצוּיָה בְּבֶן גִּילוֹ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it is not commonly found on his peer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סִימָנִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference (מאי לאו) drawn in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the mole ברייתא. It does not, by itself, settle the contradiction from Step 17.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מחלוקת can be explained without any disagreement about סימנים. It is only about whether a mole is a distinctive enough sign.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a סימן counts only if it is distinctive. A sign that many people share is not a real סימן, even for someone who holds סימנים are Torah-level.

steps.title: Second version: does a mole change after death?
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) explains the מחלוקת differently. Everyone agrees סימנים are Torah-level; they disagree about whether a mole tends to change after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: Here they disagree about whether a mole is likely to change after death. One Sage holds it is likely to change after death, and the other holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's rejection, with a different reason why the תנאים disagree about the mole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the worry is not that other people have similar moles. The worry is that a mole may look different on a dead body than it did in life, so the witness cannot be sure it is the same mole. Either way, the מחלוקת is about this specific sign, not about סימנים in general.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, in both versions, everyone holds סימנים are Torah-level. The מחלוקת about a mole is only about whether a mole is a reliable sign: either because others commonly have one, or because it may change after death.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against רבא. It is a second version of רבא's own answer: same conclusion, different reason.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Here, about whether a mole is likely to change
after death, they disagree.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: עֲשׂוּיָה לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One Sage holds: it is likely to change after death.
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who therefore does not accept testimony based on a mole.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: it is not likely to change after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: הָכָא בְּשׁוּמָא הָעֲשׂוּיָה לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the rejection in Step 20, with a different explanation of the מחלוקת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the mole ברייתא that some תנאים hold סימנים are only rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מחלוקת may be about whether a mole changes after death, not about whether סימנים are Torah-level.

steps.title: A third version: everyone holds סימנים are rabbinic, and the argument is about a mole
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבא says that everyone agrees סימנים are only דרבנן. The dispute in the ברייתא is about how to treat a mole (שומא) specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: רבא said, everyone agrees that סימנים are rabbinic. And here, the argument is about a mole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third version of how רבא rejected אביי's reading of the ברייתא. This time רבא says both sides agree that סימנים are only rabbinic, and he begins to explain that the argument is about a mole. That explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי disagree about whether סימנים are Torah-level. This version of רבא still rejects that idea, but from the opposite side: both agree that סימנים are only rabbinic. So the real disagreement must be about something special to a mole.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying marks are relied on only by rabbinic law
A mole or birthmark on the body

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the versions! In steps 20 and 21, everyone agreed סימנים are Torah-level. In this version, everyone agrees they are only rabbinic. In all of them, רבא rejects אביי's claim that the two sides argue about this question.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
phrases.notes: This is a third version of רבא's answer, after the two in steps 20 and 21.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees that identifying marks are rabbinic.
And here, it is about a mole

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סִימָנִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third version of רבא's rejection. Unlike steps 20 and 21, it assumes סימנים are only rabbinic according to everyone.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's claim from step 19 that the ברייתא shows a disagreement over whether סימנים are Torah-level or rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sides actually agree that סימנים are rabbinic. Their dispute is about something specific to a mole, not about סימנים in general.
